title: Rate Lock Commitment Extension Policy
content:
**Rate Lock Commitment extensions** — when an extension may be booked, how long it may be, where the new expiration date falls, and who bears the cost of the extension days.

### 1. When an extension may be booked

1.1 An extension is booked only while the lock status is locked.

1.2 An extension is booked only if the extension request was logged no later than the current lock expiration date. The request date of the extension request in the lock request log is compared with the lock's current expiration date. A request dated on the expiration date itself is on time; a request dated any later day is not.

1.3 An extension is booked only while the loan file status is processing, underwriting, conditionally approved, suspended or clear to close.

1.4 An expired lock can never be extended; it can only be relocked.

Each of these is read from system records for the lock and loan file concerned, before the extension is booked: the lock's status and current expiration date, the request date of the extension request in that lock's request log, and the loan file's status. A recollection of when the request was made is not a basis.

| Extension request dated | Lock's current expiration date | On time |
|---|---|---|
| The day before the expiration date | Day zero | Yes |
| The expiration date itself | Day zero | Yes |
| The day after the expiration date | Day zero | No |

### 2. Length and limits

2.1 The extension length must be one of the product's sold extension lengths.

2.2 The lock may carry at most the product's maximum number of extensions, and at most the product's maximum cumulative extension days in total. Both are counted over the life of the lock up to today: the number of extension entries booked on the lock and the sum of their extension days.

### 3. New expiration date

3.1 The new expiration date is the current lock expiration date plus the extension days in calendar days. When it lands on a Saturday, Sunday or federal public holiday, it rolls forward to the next business day.

3.2 Because extension days are always added to the current expiration date, they are never added to the request date.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a lock whose current expiration date is a Tuesday, extended by 10 days, has a new expiration date on the Friday of the following week, provided that Friday is a business day. This holds even if the request was logged several days earlier.

### 4. Cost and who bears it

4.1 *Clause no longer in force:* the former clause that the charged days are the extension days less the Larkspur-borne days, that the cost in points is the charged days times the product's extension cost per day divided by 100, and that the dollar cost is the cost in points times the loan amount at lock divided by 100, rounded to the cent. This clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis for working out an extension's cost.

4.2 *Clause no longer in force:* the former statement that Larkspur bears extension days in two cases only is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis. Under that basis the two cases are no longer the only ones in which Larkspur bears extension days.

4.3 The first extension on the lock carries up to the product's complimentary extension days as Larkspur-borne days.

4.4 *Clause no longer in force:* the former clause about appraisal delays is no longer in force for an extension booking, a waiver Larkspur books on its own initiative or a decided extension-charge dispute. Each of these measures its appraisal-delay days under the current basis, which supersedes this clause. That clause provided that when the loan's appraisal order was completed after its due date, Larkspur bears as many extension days as the appraisal was late (the completed date less the due date, in calendar days), never more than the product's lender-delay allowance borne for this reason across the lock.

4.5 When both apply, the complimentary days are counted first.

4.6 An extension with no charged days is booked with Larkspur as cost bearer and a cost of 0.00. Any other extension has the borrower as cost bearer.

4.7 Underwriting backlog, the borrower's late documents, and seller or title delays never shift the cost.

4.8 A cost booked to the borrower that is later found to qualify is waived with a waiver entry naming the original extension entry. It is never waived by editing that entry.

Larkspur bears extension days in two cases only.

Second, when the loan's appraisal order was completed after its due_date, Larkspur bears as many extension days as the appraisal was late (completed_date minus due_date in calendar days), never more than lender_delay_waiver_max_days borne for this reason across the lock.
